items.summary: Congress may make no law respecting an establishment of religion.
Congress may not prohibit free exercise of religion.
Congress may not abridge freedom of speech.
Congress may not abridge freedom of the press.
The people retain constitutional protection to peaceably assemble.
The people retain protection to petition the government for redress of grievances.
The text references a well-regulated militia as necessary to the security of a free State; doctrinal implications are separate.
The constitutional right of the people to keep and bear arms shall not be infringed, subject to controlling doctrine.
No soldier may be quartered in any house during peacetime without the owner's consent.
During war, quartering must be in a manner prescribed by law.
The people have a right to be secure in persons, houses, papers and effects against unreasonable searches and seizures.
A warrant cannot issue without probable cause supported by oath or affirmation.
Warrants must particularly describe the place to be searched and persons or things to be seized.
A person shall not be held to answer for a capital or otherwise infamous crime without grand jury presentment or indictment, subject to textual exceptions.
Text excepts cases arising in land or naval forces, or the militia when in actual service in time of war or public danger.
No person may be twice put in jeopardy of life or limb for the same offense.
No person in any criminal case shall be compelled to be a witness against themself.
No person may be deprived of life, liberty or property without due process of law by the federal government.
Private property may be taken for public use only subject to the Just Compensation Clause.
Private property taken for public use requires just compensation.
Accused persons have the right to a speedy trial in covered criminal prosecutions.
Accused persons have the right to a public trial in covered criminal prosecutions.
Covered prosecutions require an impartial jury of the State and district where crime committed; district previously ascertained by law.
The accused must be informed of the nature and cause of the accusation.
The accused has the right to be confronted with the witnesses against them.
The accused may have compulsory process for obtaining witnesses in their favor.
The accused has the right to assistance of counsel for their defense.
In suits at common law where value in controversy exceeds twenty dollars, the jury-trial right is preserved.
No fact tried by jury may be otherwise re-examined in a U.S. court than under rules of common law.
Excessive bail shall not be required.
Excessive fines shall not be imposed.
Cruel and unusual punishments shall not be inflicted.
Constitutional enumeration of certain rights shall not be construed to deny or disparage others retained by the people.
Powers not delegated to United States nor prohibited to States are reserved to States respectively.
The same undelegated and nonprohibited powers are alternatively reserved to the people.
Judicial power cannot be construed to extend to specified suits in law or equity against a State.
The express Eleventh Amendment rule concerns suits against a State commenced or prosecuted by citizens of another State or foreign citizens/subjects.
Presidential electors cast distinct ballots for President and Vice President and list each category separately.
At least one candidate voted for must not be an inhabitant of the elector's State.
Electors make, sign, certify and transmit lists of votes to the President of the Senate.
The President of the Senate opens certificates in the presence of both Houses, and votes are counted subject to enacted law.
The highest presidential vote recipient is elected President if majority of electors appointed.
Without a majority the House chooses President from no more than top three presidential electoral candidates; State delegations vote by State with special quorum and majority requirements.
Without majority for Vice President, Senate chooses from top two with two-thirds quorum and majority-of-whole-Senate requirement.
A person constitutionally ineligible to office of President is ineligible to be Vice President.
Slavery and involuntary servitude shall not exist in United States or any place subject to their jurisdiction, except for the specified conviction-based punishment clause.
The narrow original exception is punishment for crime whereof a party shall have been duly convicted; it is not a general license for slavery.
Congress may enforce the Thirteenth Amendment by appropriate legislation.
Persons born or naturalized in United States and subject to its jurisdiction are citizens of United States.
Qualified U.S. citizens are citizens of the State where they reside.
No State shall make or enforce law abridging privileges or immunities of U.S. citizens.
No State shall deprive any person of life, liberty or property without due process.
No State may deny any person within its jurisdiction equal protection of the laws.
Representatives shall be apportioned among States according to their respective numbers, with text and subsequent changes.
Original text referred to excluding 'Indians not taxed'; preserve as historical text only, not a present rule authorizing race-based exclusion.
Section 2 describes reduction of State representation for abridged/denied specified voting rights with textual exceptions and later constitutional changes.
Historical 21-year-old male citizen reference is modified by subsequent suffrage amendments including XXVI; do not treat as a modern eligibility limit.
The original apportionment vote-denial formula excepts participation in rebellion or other crime; scope requires jurisprudence.
Section 3 disqualification is tethered to a previously described oath to support Constitution and specified classes of officials.
Section 3 specifies engaging in insurrection or rebellion or giving aid or comfort to enemies, under constitutional office criteria.
Coverage includes named federal and State offices with specified oaths and prerequisites; application contested doctrine handled separately.
Congress may remove Section 3 disability by a vote of two-thirds of each House.
Validity of public debt of United States, authorized by law, including enumerated suppression of insurrection/rebellion debts, shall not be questioned.
Neither United States nor any State may assume or pay debt incurred in aid of insurrection or rebellion against United States.
Neither United States nor any State may assume or pay claims for loss or emancipation of enslaved persons; such claims are illegal and void.
Congress shall have power to enforce Fourteenth Amendment provisions by appropriate legislation.
Right of U.S. citizens to vote shall not be denied or abridged by United States or any State on account of race.
Citizens' voting rights shall not be denied or abridged on account of color.
Citizens' voting rights shall not be denied or abridged on account of previous condition of servitude.
Congress may enforce Fifteenth Amendment by appropriate legislation.
Congress has power to lay and collect taxes on incomes from whatever source derived, subject to constitutional limits.
Income taxes described by Sixteenth Amendment may be laid without apportionment among States and without regard to any census or enumeration.
The people of each State elect two Senators for six-year terms, each with one vote.
Electors in each State have qualifications requisite for electors of most numerous branch of State legislature, subject to later amendments and voting rights law.
When Senate vacancy occurs, State executive authority issues writs of election to fill vacancy.
State legislature may empower executive to make temporary Senate appointments until voters fill vacancy by election.
Original transition rule protects election or term of any Senator chosen before Amendment XVII became valid; historical transitional exception.
Repealed national ban on manufacture, sale and transport of intoxicating liquors for beverage purposes; not current constitutional authority.
Repealed amendment's substantive prohibition was deferred for one year from ratification before commencing January 1920.
Repealed Article XVIII allocated concurrent enforcement authority to Congress and States; this authority ended with repeal in 1933.
Repealed amendment's ratification prerequisite had to be satisfied within seven years and was met in 1919; not a recurring contemporary duty.
Voting rights of U.S. citizens may not be denied or abridged by United States or States on account of sex.
Congress may enforce Nineteenth Amendment by appropriate legislation.
President and Vice President terms end at noon January 20 in relevant years; successors' terms begin then.
Senator and Representative terms end at noon January 3 in relevant years; successors' terms begin then.
Congress must meet at least once annually beginning noon January 3 unless Congress by law appoints a different day.
Congress may by law appoint a different annual meeting day.
At beginning of term, if President-elect died, Vice-President-elect becomes President.
If no President chosen before term or President-elect fails qualification, Vice-President-elect acts as President until President qualifies.
Congress may by law determine who acts as President if neither a President-elect nor a Vice-President-elect qualifies, subject to text.
Contingent acting President serves only until a President or Vice President qualifies, according to the relevant section.
Congress may by law address death of a person from whom House may choose a President in a contingent election.
Congress may by law address death of a person from whom Senate may choose a Vice President in a contingent election.
Sections 1 and 2 expressly entered legal effect October 15, 1933, rather than the January 1933 ratification date.
Amendment XX required ratification by State legislatures within seven years of proposal; requirement fulfilled in 1933.
Twenty-First Amendment Section 1 repealed Amendment XVIII as of ratification December 5, 1933.
Transport/import of intoxicating liquor into a State, Territory or possession for delivery/use in violation of local law is prohibited, subject to controlling constitutional doctrine.
Twenty-First Amendment used State conventions and a seven-year ratification window; condition fulfilled December 1933.
No person may be elected President more than twice under Twenty-Second Amendment.
A person holding/acting as President for more than two years of another President's term may be elected President no more than once.
Section 1's historically specific exemptions for officeholder at proposal and within the term at adoption do not create an unlimited modern exception.
Amendment XXII's seven-year legislative ratification requirement was met in February 1951.
District constituting seat of government appoints presidential electors as Congress may direct; DC does not thereby become a State.
District receives electors equivalent to putative Senators and Representatives, but no more than least populous State.
District electors are additional to State electors and follow Twelfth Amendment presidential/vice presidential election mechanism.
Congress may enforce Twenty-Third Amendment by appropriate legislation.
Citizens' federal election voting rights cannot be denied or abridged by federal/State governments for failure to pay a poll tax or other tax.
Twenty-Fourth Amendment text covers Presidential/VP elections and electors plus U.S. Senate and House elections, including primaries.
Congress may enforce Twenty-Fourth Amendment by appropriate legislation.
Upon presidential removal, death or resignation, Vice President becomes President; separate from Acting President on inability.
If Vice Presidency vacant, President nominates a new Vice President.
Vice presidential nominee assumes office upon a majority vote of each House, not Senate-only advice and consent.
President transmits written declaration of inability to President pro tempore Senate and Speaker House.
Upon declaration, Vice President discharges powers and duties as Acting President.
President may transmit contrary written declaration to resume powers under Section 3.
Vice President and majority principal executive officers (or substitute body Congress may by law provide) submit written inability declaration.
Following the written initial Section 4 inability declaration, Vice President immediately assumes powers as Acting President.
President may declare no inability exists; Vice President with specified majority may challenge by written declaration within four days.
Following the specified contested declaration, Congress must assemble within 48 hours if not in session.
Congress must decide disputed inability within 21 days after receiving the latter declaration or after required assembly when not in session.
Continued Vice President Acting Presidency upon contested presidential ability requires a two-thirds vote of each House.
If Congress does not meet the required constitutional two-thirds determination, President resumes powers and duties.
Citizens of United States who are eighteen years of age or older have voting-right protection against age-based denial.
Neither United States nor any State may abridge covered citizens' voting rights on account of age.
Congress may enforce Twenty-Sixth Amendment by appropriate legislation.
A law varying Senators' or Representatives' compensation cannot take effect until an election of Representatives intervenes.
The original First Amendment directly restrains Congress; doctrine applying rights to States is separate and must cite cases and Fourteenth Amendment.
Prefatory militia language must not be treated as sole and complete operative rule for firearm regulation; record judicial interpretations separately.
In peacetime, owner's consent is the original express prerequisite for soldier quartering.
Wartime quartering requires a manner prescribed by law, not unrestricted military direction.
Warrants require probable cause, supported by oath or affirmation.
Warrants must particularly describe the place to search and persons or things to seize.
The original grand-jury indictment rule has the land/naval forces and militia-in-actual-service wartime/public danger exception.
Fifth Amendment due process originally binds federal governmental action; Fourteenth Amendment separately regulates States.
Jury district must include the place of offense and be previously ascertained by law.
Textually preserved civil jury right refers to suits at common law where the amount in controversy exceeds twenty dollars.
Re-examination rule concerns courts of United States; State civil jury doctrine cannot be inferred as direct original Seventh Amendment text.
Enumerating specific rights shall not deny/disparage other rights retained by people; this text alone does not identify every candidate unenumerated right.
Reservation requires power neither delegated to federal government nor prohibited to States; States and people remain distinct recipients.
Express restriction applies to suits against States by citizens of another State or foreign State's citizens/subjects, not all cases involving States.
House contingent presidential election votes by States, with quorum from two thirds of States and majority of all States necessary to choose.
Senate contingent vice presidential election needs two-thirds of whole Senate for quorum and majority of whole Senate to choose.
Vote count language does not resolve all statutory count, objection or certification procedures; modern procedures require enacted law and doctrine.
Original exception specifically conditions servitude as punishment for crime on a person being duly convicted; no general revival of slavery.
Privileges or immunities expressly concern U.S. citizens; due process and equal protection clauses separately protect persons.
State due-process guarantee extends to any person within its constitutional reach, not exclusively U.S. citizens.
State equal-protection text protects any person within its jurisdiction, not citizens alone.
The original male/21-years age formulation has later voting-rights overlays including the Twenty-Sixth Amendment.
Congress may remove the Section 3 disqualification only by two-thirds vote of each House; no candidate-specific enforcement finding is made.
Section 4 refers to public debt of United States authorized by law; it is not an executive spending appropriation.
Fifteenth Amendment vote-discrimination restrictions bind United States and any State.
Sixteenth Amendment removes an apportionment requirement for taxes on incomes described by text; does not repeal every other constitutional tax limit.
State executive temporary Senate appointments require legislative empowerment; election remains the constitutional vacancy-filling mechanism.
The prohibition was repealed on December 5, 1933 and cannot confer an operative power or prohibition.
Prohibition ratified January 16, 1919 but its delayed ban began January 17, 1920 according to CRS and ended on repeal December 5, 1933.
Section 1 became legally effective October 15, 1933; the first presidential term transition under it occurred January 20, 1937.
Section 2 became legally effective October 15, 1933; Congress's new annual session rule is distinct from ratification date.
The seven-year ratification limit of Amendment XX was fulfilled historically, not a recurring limit on contemporary constitutional amendment processes.
Amendment XXI Section 1 repeals Amendment XVIII, rather than merely modifying national prohibition in selected States.
Section 2 prohibits specified import/transport in violation of destination jurisdiction law; further commerce and nondiscrimination limits require precedent.
Ratification occurred by State conventions within the specified seven years; this completed mode and deadline are historical and not a new general requirement.
More than two years of another elected President's term as President or Acting President triggers maximum one additional election to Presidency.
The text's original grandfather class depends on contemporaneous incumbency/proposal and initial adoption; it is not a current recurring exemption.
District of Columbia presidential elector allocation may not exceed that of the least populous State; District does not become a State.
Express Twenty-Fourth Amendment poll-tax prohibition covers specified federal primaries and elections, not a verbatim federal provision on every State/local contest.
Vice-presidential vacancy nominee must be confirmed by a majority in both House and Senate; unlike ordinary Article II appointments.
After President's written ability declaration, specified counter-declaration must be transmitted within four days to contest restoration.
Congress must convene within forty-eight hours if not in session following qualifying disputed inability proceedings.
Congress must determine inability within the constitutionally described twenty-one-day period according to whether it is in session.
Continuation as Acting President under contested Section 4 inability requires two-thirds vote of both Houses of Congress.
Voting age protection attaches to citizens eighteen years of age or older, preventing denial based on age.
A law changing compensation for Senators or Representatives cannot take effect until an election of Representatives has intervened.
